cells.tense: The seeing is here now, in your own hands
cells.ask: Say out loud what you're making room for — once, to nobody in particular, in words you'd actually use. You end up with a sentence you can act from.
cells.core:
You catch what's shifting in something you care for almost before it shifts — the first small change, the thing that isn't a problem yet. It isn't a worry habit, and it isn't a performance. You look at what's there and you don't make it mean anything about you, which is why you can hold what you find without needing it to flatter you, and why the look stays usable when the news is bad.

Today, say out loud what you've been making room for, once, in your own plain words. Hearing yourself name it sharpens what you see, and the sentence stays yours to act from.
cells.sheetLine: You see it early and you don't need it to mean you.

cells.tense: You're reading a page that hasn't been written yet
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're growing and leave it alone for a full day — no checking, no adjusting, no comparing it to where it should be. You end up with a day's evidence that it kept going without your hands on it.
cells.core:
You're seeing every way this could go before it's begun. The whole season at once, each version worse than the last, and the looking ahead has swallowed the job. The thing you're tending hasn't had a quiet minute since.

When this is working, you look at what's there and let it be exactly what it is — no rehearsal, no schedule, no arriving with the verdict already drafted. Care doesn't have to look like knowing first. Pick one thing growing under your hands and leave it untouched for a day. No checking whether it's on track, no planning what you'll do if it stalls. Let it have the kind of day it would have if you weren't watching.
cells.sheetLine: You're caring for it by worrying about it, and it can't feel the difference.
cells.verb: seeing clearly — taking in what is actually there, before naming it
cells.place: in the care for what is growing, where tending happens by attention and not by force

cells.tense: The looking stopped back where it wasn't safe
cells.ask: Go stand in front of one thing you're growing — close, for a few minutes — with no plan and nothing to fix, then say out loud what's actually there. You end up with the plain state of things instead of your idea of it.
cells.core:
Looking at what you're growing used to be the easy part. You'd see it, and seeing it told you what to do next. That has gone quiet. Now you stay informed from a distance — updates, reports, other people's accounts of the thing rather than the thing itself. You know the state of it the way you know the news.

This works when you can stand close to the thing and let it show you what it is, with nothing yet decided about what you'll do next. You haven't lost the ability to do that. Standing one step back has just become where you rest. Go look. Not to fix anything, not to make a plan. Take in what's in front of you without settling anything about it.
cells.sheetLine: You're caring for it from one step back, and you can't care from there.
cells.verb: seeing clearly — taking in what is actually there, before naming it
cells.place: in the care for what is growing, where tending happens by attention and not by force

cells.tense: You're already tuned to it, and calling it nothing
cells.ask: Say out loud the one shift you've noticed in something you're tending — then, right after it, 'I'm the one who noticed that.' You end up with what you already knew, carried under your own name.
cells.core:
You already pick things up. The subtle shift in someone's mood, the turn a project took last week, the thing that changed before anyone said it changed. It comes in clearly, and it's accurate. You just file it under 'that's how it is' or 'someone would have said something.'

When this is working, you call it what it is: you noticed, and you know you did. That's the whole difference — the same clear look, only signed. Standing close enough to see it was your doing, and you did that part. What's missing is smaller than it sounds. Say the shift out loud, and put your name on having noticed it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already seeing it. You're just not signing for it.
